summary: This standards-track memo describes a convention for using the Cryptographic Message Syntax to protect a collection of content items together. Attributes can optionally be attached to the content.

eli5.summary: Instead of locking each item in its own box, this lets you put many items in one box and lock them together, with labels if you want.

questions: what is a cms content collection
what is content with attributes in cms
when to use cms content collection instead of mime multipart
subtitle: Two CMS content types for bundling several contents together, optionally with attributes, under one layer of protection.

tldr.problem: CMS protects one content at a time, and outside of MIME there was no standard way to protect a group of contents, each with its own type.
tldr.mechanism: A content-collection type holds a sequence of ContentInfo items, and a content-with-attributes type pairs one ContentInfo with a non-empty list of attributes.
tldr.outcome: A whole collection can sit inside CMS protection such as a signature. Implementations MUST be prepared to handle multiple levels of encapsulation.

today: RFC 4073 is a Proposed Standard (May 2005). The unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Why Collections Are Needed
sections.content:
RFC 4073 describes a convention for using the Cryptographic Message Syntax (RFC 3852) to protect a content collection. The content-collection content type transfers one or more contents, each identified by a content type. The content-with-attributes content type can attach arbitrary attributes to a content.

The convention is not needed when CMS is used with MIME, because MIME multipart (RFC 2045) already carries more than one content item, each with a MIME type. It is aimed at cases where CMS is used in an exclusively ASN.1 environment, where each item is identified by an object identifier instead.
sections.eli5: Email already has a way to put many attachments in one message. This document is for the other situations, where there is no such thing and you still want to bundle things up.

sections.title: The Amphora Examples
sections.content:
The RFC illustrates the need with an art collector selling an ancient Greek urn called an amphora. The signed offer has three parts: the offer for sale with the asking price, a high-quality image, and an appraisal from a ceramics expert. The expert signs the appraisal, and the collector signs the whole offer, so two SignedData layers are used.

A second example shows why attributes help. If the collector provides several images, each can carry attributes such as resolution, the date the image was taken and the photographer. The whole image collection can then replace the single image and be covered by the collector's signature.
sections.eli5: A seller packs an offer, photos and an expert's report into one box and signs it. Each photo can have a sticky note saying who took it and when.

sections.title: The Content Collection Type
sections.content:
The content-collection type is named by the object identifier id-ct-contentCollection, whose final arc is 19. Its syntax is ContentCollection ::= SEQUENCE SIZE (1..MAX) OF ContentInfo, so it holds at least one ContentInfo, one for each content. The contentType inside each ContentInfo says what that content is.

Contents can have varying levels of protection. A collection could mix CMS protection content types with unprotected ones, and it is expected, but not required, to be encapsulated in one or more CMS protecting content types.

Implementations SHOULD be prepared to handle the object identifiers for SignedData, EncryptedData, EnvelopedData and AuthenticatedData from CMS, and for CompressedData from RFC 3274.
sections.eli5: The collection is a list of wrapped items, with at least one in it. Each item says what it is, and some may be locked while others are not.

sections.title: The Content-with-Attributes Type
sections.content:
The content-with-attributes type carries a single content, identified by a content type, together with a collection of attributes about it. Its object identifier is id-ct-contentWithAttrs, whose final arc is 20.

The syntax is a SEQUENCE of content (a ContentInfo) and attrs (a SEQUENCE SIZE (1..MAX) OF Attribute). Any number of attributes is allowed, but there must be at least one. The Attribute structure was originally defined in X.501 and is repeated in CMS.
sections.eli5: This is one item with a list of sticky notes. You must stick on at least one note, and you can add as many as you like.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
Because a collection can contain contents with different levels of protection, and is only expected to be wrapped in CMS protection, implementations MUST be prepared to handle multiple levels of encapsulation.

The security considerations in RFC 3852 are relevant whenever CMS protects more than one content through either of these two content types. The RFC adds no further security rules of its own.
sections.eli5: Boxes can sit inside boxes, so a program has to be ready to open several layers. Everything that makes plain CMS safe still applies.
